title: Planning for post-quantum cryptography
summary: ACSC guidance on planning the migration to post-quantum cryptography, covering the creation and analysis of quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms.

title: Stay ahead of the quantum threat with post-quantum cryptography
summary: News item from the Australian Cyber Security Centre urging organisations to prepare for the quantum threat by adopting quantum-resistant cryptographic algorithms.

title: Information Security Manual: Guidelines for cryptography
summary: Cryptography chapter of ASD's Information Security Manual, including provisions for post-quantum algorithms and post-quantum/traditional hybrid schemes.

title: Quantum technology primer: Computing
summary: Primer on quantum computing noting that as cryptographically relevant quantum computers emerge, organisations will need to rely on post-quantum cryptography.

title: Budget estimates question on notice BE24-0018 (Legal and Constitutional Affairs)
summary: 2024-25 Budget estimates question-on-notice response stating that entities will be encouraged to prepare for the post-quantum future by reviewing data holdings and developing a plan.

title: Senate estimates committee Hansard, 2 December 2025
summary: Senate estimates committee transcript in which senators question the Home Affairs portfolio on its handling of post-quantum cryptography.

title: State of Australian Quantum Report 2024, Appendix A: Support for quantum across the Australian Government
summary: Appendix to the State of Australian Quantum Report 2024 mapping government support for quantum, noting a Plan of Action that deals explicitly with adopting post-quantum cryptographic standards.

title: National Quantum Strategy: Quantum technologies
summary: Section of Australia's National Quantum Strategy covering the spectrum of quantum technologies, including an indicative 5-to-10-year horizon for post-quantum cryptography.

title: List of Critical Technologies in the National Interest: Quantum technologies
summary: Quantum technologies entry in the List of Critical Technologies in the National Interest, naming post-quantum cryptography among priority technologies for improved data security.

title: Critical Technologies Challenge Program round 1 projects
summary: Announcement of round 1 projects funded under the Critical Technologies Challenge Program, including post-quantum cryptography supportive hardware to reduce eavesdropping risks.

title: The Quantum Safe Transition: Reality, Hurdles and Pathways
summary: CSIRO report examining why transitioning to post-quantum cryptography is a priority for Australia and the realities, hurdles and pathways of the quantum-safe transition.

title: Post quantum safe transition and cyber resilience
summary: CSIRO research programme providing guidance, tools and frameworks to identify critical assets, assess cryptographic dependencies and plan post-quantum migration pathways.

title: Quantum shift: How are Australian organisations navigating the quantum frontier?
summary: CSIRO report on how Australian organisations are navigating quantum readiness, with transitioning to post-quantum cryptography among the key focus areas of proactive organisations.

title: Australian Signals Directorate releases the Annual Cyber Threat Report 2024-25
summary: ASD news release announcing the Annual Cyber Threat Report 2024-25, urging organisations to prepare for post-quantum cryptography.

title: ASD Science, Technology, Innovation and Research Priorities
summary: ASD's published research priorities, listing mathematics and post-quantum cryptography among its priority research areas alongside quantum computing and algorithms.

title: Parliamentary inquiry document on post-quantum cryptography implementation timelines
summary: Document held in the Parliament of Australia document store stating that the time required to implement post-quantum cryptography will vary with a Commonwealth entity's cyber security posture. Issuing body is not identifiable from the listing.

title: Submission: the impact of new and emerging information and communications technologies
summary: Submission to a parliamentary inquiry on new and emerging information and communications technologies that references post-quantum encryption. Issuing body is not identifiable from the listing.

title: Enabling post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migration (industry PhD opportunity)
summary: CSIRO industry PhD project listing on developing techniques for the migration to post-quantum cryptography to secure critical infrastructure from quantum attacks.

title: Quantum technology primer: Overview
summary: Overview entry in ASD/ACSC's Quantum Technology Primer series, stating that adopting post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is a key example of preparation for quantum technologies because cryptographically relevant quantum computers will break current asymmetric cryptography.

title: Quantum technology primer: Communications
summary: Communications entry in ASD/ACSC's Quantum Technology Primer series, advising organisations to prioritise strengthening their security posture and planning for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and discussing harvest-now-decrypt-later risks.

title: Quantum technology primer: Communications (PDF)
summary: Downloadable PDF of the ASD/ACSC Quantum Technology Primer on quantum communications, noting the need to plan for post-quantum cryptography and the limits of quantum communications as a practical security solution.

title: Third release in our Quantum Technology Primer series: Communications
summary: ASD/ACSC news item announcing the third release in the Quantum Technology Primer series on quantum communications, reiterating the importance of planning for post-quantum cryptography.

title: New publication released – Quantum technology primer: Overview
summary: ASD/ACSC news item announcing release of the Quantum Technology Primer: Overview, highlighting adoption of post-quantum cryptography as a key preparation for quantum technologies.

title: Read the latest publication in our Quantum technology primer series – Quantum Computing
summary: ASD/ACSC news item announcing the Quantum Computing publication in the Quantum Technology Primer series, noting that organisations will need to rely on post-quantum cryptography as cryptographically relevant quantum computers emerge.

title: Information Security Manual: March 2026 changes
summary: ASD change log for the March 2026 release of the Information Security Manual, documenting updates to cryptography guidance including the transition to ASD-approved post-quantum algorithms (ML-DSA, ML-KEM) and timelines for ceasing traditional asymmetric cryptography.

title: Post-quantum questions to ask your vendors
summary: ASD/ACSC publication first released on 16 July 2026 setting out 31 vendor-neutral questions, aligned to the five phases of ASD's LATICE framework, that organisations can use in procurement, contract renewal and vendor assurance to assess third-party readiness for the post-quantum cryptography transition. It frames vendor readiness as one of the biggest factors influencing whether an organisation can adopt PQC within ASD's recommended timeframes.

title: Post-quantum questions to ask your vendors (PDF)
summary: Downloadable July 2026 PDF of ASD's vendor-assessment guidance for the post-quantum cryptography transition, covering cryptographic dependencies, risk assessment, transition planning, implementation approaches and communication with suppliers. Published in the cyber.gov.au 2026-07 file directory.

title: New guidance helps organisations assess vendor readiness for post-quantum cryptography
summary: ASD/ACSC news item announcing the release of 'Post-quantum questions to ask your vendors', restating that the ISM recommends ceasing traditional asymmetric cryptography by end of 2030 and that organisations should have a refined PQC transition plan by end of 2026. It stresses that vendors often control cryptographic mechanisms in cloud and managed-service environments, making vendor readiness decisive for PQC migration.

title: APRA Member Therese McCarthy Hockey's remarks to the 2026 AFIA Risk Summit
summary: Speech delivered on 24 June 2026 in Melbourne in which APRA Member Therese McCarthy Hockey sets out the prudential regulator's expectations on the quantum threat, endorsing ASD's timeline that organisations have a post-quantum cryptography transition plan by end of 2026 and have commenced transition by end of 2028. She states that APRA will step up supervisory engagement, expects regulated entities to map cryptographic dependencies across systems, data and third-party providers, and wants evidence that boards understand the risk and are advancing migration plans.

title: Information security manual (June 2026)
summary: Consolidated June 2026 release of ASD's Information Security Manual, whose Guidelines for cryptography carry the ASD-approved post-quantum algorithm set (ML-KEM-768/1024, ML-DSA-87) and the requirement that new cryptographic equipment, applications and libraries support these algorithms by no later than 2030. This release also renamed the 'data protection' cyber security principle to 'cryptographic protection' and retains principle PRO-17 on cryptographic agility, which explicitly covers changes to post-quantum cryptography.

title: Quantum technology primer: Sensing
summary: Fourth entry (published 24 June 2026) in ASD/ACSC's Quantum Technology Primer series for cyber security leaders, covering how quantum sensing works, emerging applications across industries such as mining, and cyber security risks including sensor spoofing, noise sensitivity, integration and data management. Flagged for human review: unlike the Overview, Computing and Communications primers already in the corpus, an explicit post-quantum/quantum-safe cryptography reference in this primer could not be verified because cyber.gov.au would not serve the page to the fetcher.

title: APRA Corporate Plan 2026-27: Our strategic objectives
summary: Strategic objectives section of APRA's Corporate Plan 2026-27. Under cyber risks from frontier AI and quantum computing, it cites ASD's recommendation to have a PQC transition plan by the end of 2026 and start implementing it by the end of 2028, and says APRA expects regulated entities to make timely progress and will increase its focus on quantum computing risks.

title: Financial Stability Review: October 2026
summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia's October 2026 Financial Stability Review, assessing risks to the Australian financial system. In its discussion of operational and technology risks, it warns that quantum decryption will become a growing threat if post-quantum cryptography is not implemented early enough.

title: Resilience, Innovation and the Future of the Payments System
summary: Speech by RBA Assistant Governor (Financial System) Brad Jones at the AusPayNet Summit on 16 December 2025. It flags harvest-now-decrypt-later risks from quantum computing and says the Payments System Board supports migrating card payments to AES as a quantum-safe solution. The Board expects AES to be ready for use by 2030 and plans to consult on using RBA standard-setting powers under the PSRA to support the migration.

title: Blueprint for Secure Cloud: Microsoft Edge for Business
summary: ASD Blueprint for Secure Cloud configuration guidance for Microsoft Edge for Business. It notes that Edge enables hybrid post-quantum key agreement by default, consistent with ISM-1996, and advises considering a preference for quantum-safe algorithms (ML-KEM-1024 per ISM-1995) within a post-quantum cryptography transition plan (ISM-2073).
